questions.text: Which ancient people built the Great Pyramids of Giza?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: ancient Egyptians.

questions.text: Who led Nazi Germany during World War II?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Hitler.

questions.text: In what year did World War II end?
Which explorer reached the Americas in 1492?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Columbus, Cristóbal Colón.

questions.text: Which French emperor was defeated at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Napoleon, Napoleon I.

questions.text: Who led India's nonviolent struggle for independence from Britain?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Gandhi, Mohandas Gandhi. Not Indira Gandhi, a later prime minister.

questions.text: Which Italian Renaissance artist painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Leonardo, da Vinci.

questions.text: Which Egyptian queen, according to legend, died from the bite of an asp?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Cleopatra VII.

questions.text: Which ancient empire built the Colosseum?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Romans, Rome, ancient Rome.

questions.text: Which Japanese city was hit by the first atomic bomb used in war, in 1945?
questions.hostNotes: Not Nagasaki, which was bombed three days later.

questions.text: Which South African leader spent 27 years in prison before becoming president?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Mandela, Madiba.

questions.text: Which German city was divided by a wall from 1961 to 1989?
Which Jewish teenager's diary, written while hiding from the Nazis, became world-famous?
Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.hostNotes: It was dedicated in New York in 1886.

questions.text: Genghis Khan founded which empire?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Mongols, Mongolia.

questions.text: During the Cold War, the United States' main rival was which country?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: USSR, Soviet Russia.

questions.text: Which Roman leader was assassinated on the Ides of March in 44 BC?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Caesar.

questions.text: Which British prime minister led the country through most of World War II?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Churchill.

questions.text: What plague killed millions of people in 14th-century Europe?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: bubonic plague, the plague.

questions.text: Which South American civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Incas, Inca Empire. Not the Aztecs or Maya.

questions.text: Which Macedonian king built an empire stretching to India before he turned 33?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Alexander III of Macedon.

questions.text: Who led the Soviet Union during World War II?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Stalin. Not Lenin, who died in 1924.

questions.text: Which French teenager led armies in the Hundred Years' War and was burned at the stake?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Jeanne d'Arc, St. Joan.

questions.text: What name is given to the Allied landings in Normandy on June 6, 1944?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Operation Overlord, Operation Neptune.

questions.text: Who founded the People's Republic of China in 1949?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Mao, Mao Tse-tung, Chairman Mao.

questions.text: What Paris fortress-prison was stormed on July 14, 1789?
questions.hostNotes: The event marks the start of the French Revolution. July 14 is France's national day.

questions.text: The legendary Hanging Gardens were said to be in which ancient city?
The 1919 Treaty of Versailles formally ended which war?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: First World War, WWI, the Great War.

questions.text: What was the code name of the US-led project that built the first atomic bombs?
Whose assassination in Sarajevo in 1914 set off the chain of events leading to a global war?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Franz Ferdinand. He was heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne.

questions.text: What ancient network of trade routes linked China to the Mediterranean?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Silk Route, Silk Roads.

questions.text: Which Soviet nuclear power plant exploded in 1986, in what is now Ukraine?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Chornobyl.

questions.text: What 1215 English charter limited the powers of King John?
questions.hostNotes: Latin for "Great Charter".

questions.text: The Rosetta Stone was the key to deciphering what ancient writing system?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: hieroglyphs, hieroglyphics.

questions.text: Which Carthaginian general famously crossed the Alps with war elephants?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Hannibal Barca. Not Hannibal Lecter.

questions.text: Which Portuguese explorer was the first to sail from Europe to India, in 1498?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: da Gama.

questions.text: Which Russian royal dynasty was overthrown in 1917, its last tsar's family executed in 1918?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Romanovs, House of Romanov. The last tsar was Nicholas II.

questions.text: Which Soviet leader introduced the policies of glasnost and perestroika?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Gorbachev.

questions.text: What was the name of the great fleet Spain sent against England in 1588?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Armada, Invincible Armada.

questions.text: During the Seven Years' War, which country briefly occupied Manila from 1762 to 1764?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Britain, England, the British.

questions.text: What Aztec capital stood where Mexico City is today?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Tenochtitlán.

questions.text: Which ancient Mesopotamian king is famous for a law code based on "an eye for an eye"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Hammurapi.

questions.text: Which first emperor of China was buried with the Terracotta Army?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Qin Shi Huangdi, Shi Huangdi, Ying Zheng.

questions.text: Which Chinese admiral led huge "treasure fleets" across the Indian Ocean in the early 1400s?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Cheng Ho.

questions.text: In which city was ASEAN founded in 1967, with the Philippines as a founding member?
questions.hostNotes: Signed as the Bangkok Declaration. The five founders: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
